messages:
jane_acme: hey support — starting yesterday after a traffic spike we see intermittent 429s and big tail latency (500-900ms) on chat completions. burst was ~150 rps for ~10s. not seeing remaining tokens hit zero. we use per-user KV prefix keys. possible kv-cache issue?

support-bot: (ticket created) 📥 ticket#4682 assigned to devon

devon: thanks @jane_acme. can you paste one raw response headers + a request-id and a short snippet of the backend log around the 429? also how many unique prefixes in that burst?

jane_acme: headers i captured: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 6000`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 5910`, `X-Request-ID: r-8c2a1e` — so not a strict quota exhausted case. unique prefixes during repro ~120 in that 10s window. backend log (redacted):
```
[2026-02-18T14:12:03Z] r-8c2a1e INFO req=start user=jane_acme prefix=/user/alpha/123 kvcache=miss prefetch=1
[2026-02-18T14:12:03Z] r-8c2a1e DEBUG batch_wait_ms=42 batch_size=16 queue_len=17
[2026-02-18T14:12:04Z] r-8c2a1e WARN token_latency_ms=622 kv_evict=true
[2026-02-18T14:12:05Z] r-8c2a1e ERROR returned=429 reason="burst_throttle"
```

maya: quick read — this looks like classic "perceived throttling" from KV cache churn + continuous batching. short version: many unique prefixes -> lots of cold kv misses -> per-request compute spikes -> continuous batching groups those slower requests -> head-of-line blocking and increased wait times -> clients hit their retry/timeout thresholds and retry -> effective concurrency jumps -> service returns 429s or burst_throttle. :thinking_face:

alex: adding data point — our batcher has max_batch_latency_ms=10 in prod by default. if cold misses stretch token latency by 200-600ms, queued requests pile up increasing queue_len, which surfaces as apparent throttling. you can see `batch_wait_ms=42` in the log, not huge but with many miss+evicts it compounds.

sre_oncall: suggestion for short-term mitigation: 1) enable tenant-specific kvcache warmup (we can prefetch top prefixes for that org) 2) bump max_concurrency for the tenant during business hours 3) ask client to add small jitter/exponential backoff on 5xx/429 and increase client timeout window.

devon: repro steps that would replicate what we saw (from our lab):
```bash
# 200 concurrent clients, each using a unique user prefix
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rwd-chat-1","input":"hello","prefix":"/user/test'$i'"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat &
done
wait
```
python quick repro (concurrent futures):
```python
import requests, concurrent.futures
URL = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat'
def call(i):
    return requests.post(URL, json={"model":"rwd-chat-1","input":"hi","prefix":f"/user/test{i}"}, headers={"Authorization":f"Bearer {TOKEN}"})
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=200) as p:
    list(p.map(call, range(200)))
```

maya: root cause checklist:
- high prefix cardinality -> low KV hit rate
- KV prefetch config too conservative for burst pattern (prefetch_n=1)
- small batch timeout -> more head-of-line when some reqs are slow
- client retry semantics amplifying burst

devon: recommended actions (prioritized):
1) server-side quick: enable tenant warmup + set kv_prefetch_n=3 for jane_acme (we can flip flag now)
2) server-side medium: increase kvcache capacity for that tenant and enable soft-prefetch smoothing (reduces churn)
3) client-side: reduce parallel unique prefixes per second (pool session ids), add jittered backoff, increase request timeout to 2s for chat streaming setup
4) longer term: consider prefix-hashing to reduce cardinality, or use a session-affinity key so hot users reuse cache entries

jane_acme: sounds good. can you flip the warmup flag now? also curious — will increasing max_batch_latency_ms help or make it worse?

sre_oncall: we can flip warmup now for your tenant. on batch latency: raising max_batch_latency_ms trades off increased per-request latency for higher throughput and fewer small batches. for your case, moderate increase (10->30ms) reduced queue churn in our internal tests. don't go too high or streaming experience degrades.

alex: also watch these metrics while testing: `kv_hit_rate`, `batch_wait_ms_p50/p95`, `queue_len`, `token_latency_ms_p95`, and `throttle_reasons` tag. we'll monitor after warmup flip.

devon: flipping warmup flag now for tenant jane_acme (kv_prefetch_n=3, kv_warmup=true). give me 10m and repro steps and we will tail logs.

jane_acme: reproducing now with our script, will update in ~5m. thanks all. :pray:

(5m later)
jane_acme: after warmup flip we see a drop in 429s (was ~8/min during bursts, now ~0-1/min) and p95 latency down ~150ms. kv_hit_rate went from 12%->46% in our metrics. looks much better.

devon: great — we'll keep warmup on for 24h and then evaluate. follow-ups: if you still get sporadic spikes, send a few `X-Request-ID`s and we can pull the full trace.

maya: note for docs/Runbook: add a section on "perceived throttling due to KV cache churn + batching" with these mitigations. this pattern keeps cropping up.

jane_acme: appreciated, will keep monitoring and report back.

support-bot: ticket#4682 status=monitoring assignee=devon
